Allergies:
Keflex / Penicillins / Erythromycin Base / Demerol / Ceclor

Chief Complaint:
Pleuritic chest pain

History of Present Illness:
Ms. ___ is a ___ lady with COPD, ulcerative colitis, 
diverticulosis s/p partial colectomy, and 2 PE's in the past on 
chronic Warfarin with IVC filter who presented to the ED for 
chest pain and was found to have PEs and pneumonia.  

Starting at 11PM last night, She intermittently has chest pain, 
but this pain is worse since 11PM last over the past 2 hours.  
It is left-sided, sharp, worse with coughing.  Not related to 
cughing, not worse in any specific position.  She was at her 
baseline level of shortness of breath.  Has chronic leg edema 
but no worse than usual.  No fevers, chills, nausea, vomiting, 
diaphoresis.  Cough productive of yellow sputum and has been 
ongoing for weeks, no acute change.  No change in recent 
albuterol use.   Lightheaded when standing but otherwise no 
lightheadedness, dizziness, recent falls or syncope.  She felt 
that she probably had pneumonia or a PE so she came to the ED.  

In the ED, initial VS were: 8 99.4 92 93/55 18 96% 4L Nasal 
Cannula.  She had coarse rhochi on the right and reduced air 
movement bilaterally.  Labs were notable for WBC 11.6, INR 2.8.  
CXR suggested PNA so she was given Vanc/Levo.  During the exam 
patient becoming more confused and BP dropped to ___ 
remained low consistently.  2 large bore PIVs placed and she 
received 3L NS with some improvement, but she again dropped her 
SBP to the 70's.  A RIJ CVL was placed and NE was started due to 
concern for septic shock.  Given her history of recurrent PE's 
she underwent CTA which showed acute PE's in the segmental 
anterior and posterior segments of the right superior lobar 
artery, also LLL infiltrate.  She was not started on 
anticoagulation because of a documented "Heparin and Lovenox 
allergy" which was GI bleed in the setting of receiving Heparin 
for her previous PE's when she has active colitis.  Given her 
hypotension requiring pressors, she was admitted to the MICU.  
VS prior to transfer were: HR 71, BP 132.63, RR 16, POx 96% 2L 
(92% RA) on Levophed ___.
  
On arrival to the MICU, she is comfortable.  Still has ___ 
chest discomfort and is asking for pain medications.  Her NE has 
been shut off and her BP is stable.
  
Review of systems:  
(+) Per HPI  
(-) Denies fever, chills, night sweats, recent weight loss or 
gain. Denies headache, sinus tenderness, rhinorrhea or 
congestion. Denies palpitations or weakness. Denies nausea, 
vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal pain, or changes in 
bowel habits. Denies dysuria, frequency, or urgency. Denies 
arthralgias or myalgias. Denies rashes or skin changes.

Brief Hospital Course:
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE
___ female with COPD, ulcerative colitis, diverticulosis s/p 
partial colectomy, and 2 PE's in the past on chronic Warfarin 
with IVC filter who presented to the ED for chest pain and was 
found to have PEs and pneumonia

--Active issues--

#Pulmonary embolus: Ms. ___ has h/o 2 PEs in past and had IVC 
filter placed in ___.  At admission, her INR was 3.1 and she 
was found to have a PE on CTA chest.  She has had an extensive 
hypercoag workup in the past which was unrevealing, however she 
has some degree of hypercoaguability by nature of having 
ulcerative colitis.  She was initially started on a heparin drip 
and Coumadin was held.  Heparin drip was transitioned to 
Loevenox 80mg (1mg/kg) sc q12h given that she had a PE on 
therapeutic coumadin.  IVC filter is ___ year old and no longer 
effective in preventing PE.  Anti-Xa level was 1.26 at 
discharge, Lovenox dose will be adjusted as an outpatient.  
Heme/onc was consulted and antiphosphopipid antibody was sent 
which is pending at discharge.  TTE was performed which showed 
normal EF and no evidence of right heart dysfunction.  She will 
need age appropriate cancer screening as an outpatient, 
including mammogram and colonoscopy as appropriate.  CT 
abd/pelvis showed no evidence of abdominal or pelvic malignancy 
but noted thrombus in the IVC filter.

#Hypotension: Required Norepinephrine in the ED and was 
initially admitted to the MICU, she had a triple lumen IJ 
placed.  BP was stable off pressors since arriving in the MICU.  
Her PE's are small, with no evidence of RV dysfunction/strain 
and no cardiac biomarker elevation, so her PE is an unlikely 
cause for the hypotension.  Similarly, no other obvious signs of 
sepsis to explain hypotension.  After 3L IVF, her BP was much 
improved.  She did not require any further BP support and was 
transferred to the floor where her BP remained stable in the 
90-110s.  Her Lasix and atenolol were initially held, Lasix 
restarted with no hypotension.  Atenolol will be restarted at 
the time of discharge.

#Chest pain: Left-sided pleuritic pain may be related to LLL 
PNA.  Less likely to be from right-sided PE.  Initially, the 
pain was not classic for ischemia and troponin was negative.  
She was ruled out for MI and her pain was treated with Tylenol 
and Morphine/Vicodin.  She had two additional episodes of 
crushing chest pain (noted to be different and separate from her 
initial pleuritic pain) on the floor with no acute EKG changes 
and an unremarkable CXR.  All EKGs this admission show Q waves 
in the inferior leads which were not present on her prior EKGs 
from many years ago.  Atenolol was restarted at discharge and 
she was started on an enteric coated ASA 81mg daily.

#Community Acquired PNA: No fevers but leukocytosis and LLL 
infiltrate suggested PNA. She had been given Vanc/Levo in the 
ED, but she has no recent hospitalizations and will receive 
treatment for CAP.  She completed a 5 day course of levofloxacin 
as an inpatient.

#Leg edema: Patient reports history of CHF, but EF was normal on 
echo this admission.  Her edema worsened somewhat after holding 
her Lasix.  Other potential causes for her leg edema include 
thrombus that was noted over her IVC filter or chronic venous 
insufficiency from recurrent DVT in her ___ over many years.

#COPD: She was continued on her home inhalers.  O2 sat was noted 
to drop to 85% with ambulation and she was arranged for home O2 
to wear with ambulation or activity.

--Inactive issues--

#Ulcerative Colitis: No diarrhea or bloody bowel movements 
during this admission.  As mentioned above, likely contributing 
to her pro-coagulant state.  She was continued on Asacol and 
dicyclomine.

#Schizoaffective disorder: Continued on her home Cymbalta, 
Alprazolam, Risperidone, Trazodone.  Mood was stable.

#Code status this admission: FULL CODE

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
# Needs mammogram, colonoscopy and age-appropriate cancer 
screening as outpatient
# Labs pending at the time of discharge: antiphosopholipid 
antibody, beta-2-globulin
# Started on home oxygen
# Started on ASA 81mg daily
# Started on Lovenox 80mg sc bid, will follow-up with heme/onc 
and dose will be titrated based on anti-Xa level

Discharge Diagnosis:
Primary diagnoses:
Pulmonary embolism
Community acquired pneumonia
